screening_decisions.reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in adults ≥60 years, but the outcomes assessed are influenza efficacy (culture-confirmed influenza), safety, and immunogenicity only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed as outcomes.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly individuals, but the outcomes are serological influenza, clinical influenza, and self-reported influenza only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is an RCT of H5N1 pre-pandemic vaccine vs placebo, but outcomes are immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, safety, and lot consistency only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is a randomized PROBE study of influenza vaccine vs no treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome (CVD population). The primary endpoint was a composite of major cardiovascular events including death, hospitalization from ACS, hospitalization from heart failure, and hospitalization from stroke. This meets all selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing different dosages/formulations of H1N1 influenza vaccines, but outcomes are immunogenicity (seroprotection rates) and safety only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in healthy people aged 65-74 years (specifically excluding those with chronic heart disease). Outcomes are influenza diagnosis and cost-effectiveness indicators. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed as outcomes.

This is a substudy of the FLUCAD RCT focusing only on antibody response (immunogenicity) to influenza vaccine in patients with coronary artery disease. While the parent FLUCAD study assessed cardiovascular outcomes, this specific substudy only reports on humoral immune response, not cardiovascular death or events.

This is an observational prospective cohort study, not a randomized controlled trial. It compares vaccinated vs unvaccinated individuals from administrative databases. While it mentions cardiac failure hospitalizations, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is an RCT comparing intranasal vs intramuscular influenza vaccine formulations in healthy adults. Outcomes are immunogenicity (HI antibody titers) and tolerability only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is an RCT comparing high-dose vs standard-dose influenza vaccine in adults ≥65 years. Outcomes are safety (SAEs), immunogenicity (HAI titers), and relative efficacy against influenza only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is an RCT primarily comparing two RSV vaccine formulations given with influenza vaccine in persons ≥65 years with cardiopulmonary disease. Outcomes are RSV vaccine immunogenicity, safety, and respiratory illnesses. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is a controlled study of influenza vaccine effects on warfarin anticoagulation in 69 warfarin recipients. Outcomes are INR values and anticoagulant control only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

This is a before-after experimental study with a control group evaluating the impact of a vaccination campaign strategy on vaccination coverage and cardiovascular prevention service coverage. It is not an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo/no treatment, and does not assess cardiovascular death or events as clinical outcomes.

This is a case-control study (observational design), not a randomized controlled trial. It compares vaccination status between stroke/TIA patients and population controls. While it assesses stroke risk, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is a randomized single-blind study of influenza vaccination vs control in myocardial infarction patients and PCI patients (CVD population). Primary outcomes include cardiovascular death and a triple composite endpoint of cardiovascular ischemic events. This meets all selection criteria for an RCT assessing cardiovascular outcomes in CVD patients.

This is an ecological study comparing two different vaccination programme strategies (risk disease-based vs age-based) at the population level across municipalities. It is not an individual-level RCT. While it mentions cardiovascular hospitalizations, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in Chinese elderly, but primary outcomes are immunogenicity (seroprotection rates, GMTs). While it mentions unplanned hospital admissions were lower in vaccinated group, these are general hospital admissions, not specifically cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events as defined outcomes.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in patients on vitamin K antagonists. Primary outcomes are INR values, warfarin dose variation, and hemorrhagic/thrombotic events related to anticoagulation. While thrombotic events are mentioned, the study focuses on coagulation parameters rather than cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events as primary outcomes.

This is an RCT of FluMist (LAIV) vs intranasal placebo given in addition to inactivated influenza vaccine in seniors with chronic cardiovascular or pulmonary conditions. Outcomes are safety and tolerability (reactogenicity symptoms) only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were assessed.

Despite the title suggesting relevance, the abstract describes this as a methodological paper introducing systematic review and meta-analysis techniques. It is not an RCT of influenza vaccination, but rather a tutorial on meta-analysis methodology using an example dataset.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo, but the outcomes assessed are influenza illness and immune responses (serum HI titers, IgA), not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events.
This RCT compares one dose vs two doses of influenza vaccine (not vaccine vs placebo/no treatment), and outcomes are immune responses only, not cardiovascular events.
This is a review article discussing the biologic basis and epidemiologic evidence for a causal relationship between influenza and CVD. It is not an RCT.
This RCT compares two different influenza vaccines (adjuvanted vs non-adjuvanted), not vaccine vs placebo/no treatment. Outcomes are influenza infection rates, not cardiovascular events.
This RCT compares concomitant vs sequential administration of Tdap and influenza vaccines. Outcomes are immunogenicity and safety, not cardiovascular events.
This RCT compares two types of influenza vaccines (split-virion vs subunit), not vaccine vs placebo/no treatment. Outcomes are immunogenicity and safety, not cardiovascular events.
This is an RCT of LAIV vs placebo, but outcomes are febrile illness, work loss, and health care use - not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events.
This RCT compares inactivated vs live attenuated influenza vaccines vs placebo, but outcomes are influenza prevention efficacy, not cardiovascular events.
This RCT compares cell culture-derived vs egg-based influenza vaccines, not vaccine vs placebo/no treatment. Outcomes are immunogenicity and safety, not cardiovascular events.
This RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo assesses oculorespiratory syndrome symptoms, not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events.
This RCT assesses safety and immunogenicity (antibody titers) of TIV in previously vaccinated adults. Outcomes are not cardiovascular events.
This RCT evaluates concomitant PCV13+TIV administration. Outcomes are pneumococcal immunogenicity, not cardiovascular events.
This RCT of H1N1 vaccine vs placebo assesses immunogenicity and safety outcomes, not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events.
This RCT compares concomitant vs sequential administration of Tdap-IPV and influenza vaccine. Outcomes are immunogenicity and safety, not cardiovascular events.
This is a CDC recommendation/guideline document, not an RCT.
This is a CDC recommendation/guideline document, not an RCT.
This is a review/meta-analysis article discussing existing evidence on influenza vaccination and CVD. It is not an RCT.
This is a meta-analysis pooling data from 5 trials. While it addresses cardiovascular outcomes, it is not itself an RCT.
This is a modeling/projection paper about global mortality trends. It is not an RCT and does not address influenza vaccination effects on cardiovascular outcomes.
This is a case-control study examining influenza vaccination and recurrent MI. While it addresses cardiovascular outcomes, it is not an RCT.
Observational cohort study, not an RCT. Used administrative data from managed-care organizations with multivariable logistic regression to compare vaccinated vs unvaccinated subjects.
Observational cohort study pooling data from 18 cohorts, not an RCT. Used logistic regression to estimate vaccine effectiveness.
Review article summarizing literature, not a primary RCT. States 'This review outlines the importance of vaccination and summarizes the available literature'.
Commentary/opinion piece discussing controversies in vaccine effectiveness research, not an RCT.
Population-based case-control study, not an RCT. Cases identified from paramedic reports, controls via random digit dialing.
Self-controlled case series study using within-person comparisons, not an RCT. Assessed safety (no increase in risk) rather than cardiovascular benefit.
Meta-analysis of RCTs, not a primary RCT itself. Systematically reviewed and pooled data from 5 published and 1 unpublished RCTs.
Systematic review including meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Examined 42 publications describing 39 studies.
Time series ecological study using Poisson regression, not an RCT. Did not involve vaccination intervention.
Self-controlled case series study, not an RCT. Investigated infection as trigger for AMI, not vaccination effect on cardiovascular outcomes.
RCT but assessed wrong outcomes. Primary outcome was graft rejection (biopsy grades), not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events.
Abstract does not match title - describes exercise program for chronic fatigue syndrome, not influenza vaccination for cardiovascular outcomes.
RCT but assessed wrong outcomes. Primary outcomes were safety and immunogenicity (GMTs, seroprotection rates), not cardiovascular death or events.
Non-randomized controlled prospective study, not an RCT. Outcome was influenza-like illness, not cardiovascular events.
RCT but assessed wrong outcomes. Primary outcome was antibody response (HAU titers), not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events.
Book chapter about systematic review search methods, not a research study.
